long_biography.plain_text:
Halabi moved from Syria to London as a teenager with substantial backing from his father's industrial and agricultural fortune. He began directing property companies, then used family trusts and commercial borrowing to acquire large office buildings and prestige estates. The strategy concentrated on prime locations, long corporate tenancies and redevelopment opportunities.

By the mid-2000s, the portfolio extended across central London and into leisure assets such as the Esporta health-club chain. Falling valuations exposed its dependence on debt, triggering defaults, disposals and Halabi's personal bankruptcy in 2010. The collapse reduced the scale of the business and separated the value of trust-held properties from claims about his personal fortune.
